text:
Mercedes-Benz has revealed the next GLA with two all-electric models, the 268-hp GLA 250+ Electric and the 349-hp GLA 350 4MATIC Electric. Both use an 85 kWh usable NMC pack, claim up to 657 km of WLTP range and charge at up to 320 kW on 800-volt stations. US sales start in the first half of 2028.

The release, as issued by Mercedes-Benz

Confident: striking appearance with sporty character and illuminated grille Built for every lifestyle: available with up to 657 km1 of all-electric range and 800-volt fast charging, or as a hybrid with 48-volt technology Elevated: new interior experience with more space, refinement, enhanced comfort and intelligent support that feels natural and intuitive

Stuttgart. The all-new Mercedes-Benz GLA SUV combines sporty design, advanced technology and everyday practicality. A sleeker silhouette, longer wheelbase and an available illuminated grille create a distinctly sporty and confident presence. The completely redesigned interior brings more light, space and refinement to every journey, with elevated materials, standard panoramic glass roof and an optional MBUX Superscreen. Intelligent technologies, including the MBUX Virtual Assistant powered by generative AI, provide intuitive interaction and personalized support. The 2028 Mercedes-Benz GLA will be available with both all-electric and hybrid powertrains. The GLA Hybrid variants arrive at U.S. dealerships in the second half of 2027, followed by the GLA Electric models in the first half of 2028.

The “Welcome home” feeling takes on a fresh, lifestyle-oriented character in the all-new GLA. Elevated comfort and an intuitive digital environment create an experience that feels instantly familiar. Since Carl Benz invented the automobile 140 years ago, Mercedes-Benz has continued to drive innovation forward with one clear purpose: to create tangible value for customers. With the all-new GLA, this pioneering spirit enters a new chapter.

“The new GLA is designed to excite customers every day. Drawing on 140 years of innovation, we’ve built the most expressive GLA ever. Combined with a newlydesigned interior that brings even more space and comfort, we’ve further elevated the appeal of what is already our best-selling compact model.”

Ola Källenius, Chairman of the Board of Management, Mercedes-Benz Group AG

The all-new Mercedes-Benz GLA: Key Facts

Sporty proportions: A sleek silhouette, longer wheelbase, wider rear track, pronounced muscular shoulders and wheels positioned flush with the body – the all-new GLA has a distinctly more dynamic appearance.

Charismatic presence: The all-new electric GLA brings the iconic grille to the compact segment. The striking illuminated grille contributes to the SUV’s confident presence.

Individuality is key: The all-new GLA offers customers more options for personalization, including the new ultra-sporty AMG Line Plus with Night Package and the exclusive Night Edition.

Functionality in perfect form: A high-quality interior blends floating forms, carefully selected materials and the optional large MBUX Superscreen – spanning the entire dashboard and integrating driver, central and passenger digital displays. The optional Burmester® 3D Surround Sound System delivers an impressive audio experience.

More space for everyday life and adventures: The all-new GLA offers more headroom and legroom in every seat. There’s also more space for luggage thanks to the spacious interior and versatile split-folding rear seats.

Ready for adventure: With available 4MATIC all-wheel drive, TERRAIN drive program and “Transparent Hood” function, the all-new GLA is ready for any adventure, even off the beaten path.

Effortless electric driving: With up to 657 kilometers of electric range (WLTP)1, the all-new electric GLA offers impressive long-distance comfort. Thanks to 800-volt technology, it can charge up to 270 kilometers of range (WLTP)2 in as little as 10 minutes.

Hybrid drive: The all-new GLA will also be available as a hybrid with 48-volt technology. The hybrid powertrain enables the GLA to drive on electric power in city driving, depending on the driving situation, and recuperate energy in every gear.

Intuitive and intelligent: The MBUX Virtual Assistant, powered by generative AI, can hold complex, multi-part conversations, has short-term memory and uses the latest voice technology. As a result, it sounds and responds like a well-informed friend.

Always on the right track: Thanks to the Google Cloud Automotive AI Agent, the MBUX Virtual Assistant is also well-versed in navigation-related questions. It can access information from the Google Maps platform to provide users with personalized answers to questions about navigation, points of interest and more, all through a seamless, natural conversation.

Driver assistance technologies3: The all-new GLA is equipped standard with a number of advanced driver assistance features, including Digital Extra: Distance Assist DISTRONIC4. Further expanded driver assistance systems are also optionally available.

Confident: A design statement for city life

Striking appearance with a decidedly sporty character

The silhouette alone makes it unmistakably clear: the all-new Mercedes-Benz GLA is designed to impress. The powerful SUV proportions with upright front end and flat-angle windshield present themselves in a much more dynamic form. Compared with its predecessor, the new GLA is 0.8 inches lower. Together with a longer wheelbase (+2.4 inches), wider rear track, muscular shoulders and available 18-, 19- and 20-inch wheels positioned flush with the body, the all-new SUV is ready for any adventure.

The clean, surface-oriented design with minimalist lines reinforces the sporty, confident appearance. Striking character lines and powerful surfaces create a dynamic interplay of light and shadow when viewed from the side. Full-width wheelarch trim (depending on vehicle equipment) and visual underguard at the front and rear emphasize the SUV’s rugged character. Chrome trim elements at the front and rear add exclusive touches.

Expressive front design with illuminated iconic grille

The all-new electric GLA is the first Mercedes-Benz model in the compact segment to feature the new iconic grille. It lends the GLA a unique, charismatic presence, thereby underpinning its exceptional status among compact premium SUVs. It features a chrome frame, illuminated surround, illuminated panel grille with a smoked-glass-effect mesh structure and integrated central Mercedes-Benz star. The mesh structure contains a total of 608 polycarbonate light points, which are backlit. These can also be animated as an option. Together with 158 micro-LEDs, these orchestrate light sequences that radiate in time with the Aura sound of the selected soundscape – an emotional and enthusiastic welcome.

The all-new GLA Hybrid features the star grille. A total of 150 hot-stamped chrome stars form the distinctive Mercedes-Benz pattern. An LED surround frames the radiator grille and the central Mercedes-Benz star is also illuminated.

Exterior lighting featuring star design

The standard High Performance LED headlamps provide a striking and distinctive appearance both day and night. These feature the Mercedes-Benz star as a chrome design element. With the optional LED Intelligent Light System, the daytime running lights feature the star design. Together with the illuminated grille, this creates an unmistakable light signature. The taillights are visually connected through a design element that emphasizes the width of the GLA. On vehicles equipped with the optional LED Intelligent Light System, this rear center element also features welcome and farewell animations.

AMG Line and AMG Line Plus with Night Package for a distinctly sporty look

With the optional AMG Line, the all-new GLA features AMG exterior styling including a front fascia with large air intakes, rear fascia finished in body color, wheelarch trims finished in body color and available 19- and 20-inch AMG wheels. Inside, the AMG Line adds a number of sporty accents, such as AMG sport seats, multifunction sport steering wheel in Nappa leather with flattened bottom and steering wheel paddles, available trim elements in Carbon Grain Aluminum, among other finishes, and AMG sport pedals in brushed stainless steel with black rubber studs.

The AMG Line Plus with Night Package is introduced as an option on the GLA for the first time. It builds on the AMG Line to further elevate the GLA with additional exterior design elements such as a black AMG spoiler lip, black trim elements on the side sill panels and exclusive 20-inch AMG wheels. When the front doors are opened, an animated projection with the Mercedes-Benz star pattern welcomes customers. Unique touches in the interior include exclusive MANUFAKTUR red seatbelts, Dark Shadow climate control air vent accents and illuminated door sills.

Night Edition

The new optional Night Edition gives the all-new GLA a particularly striking, sporty appearance with a number of exclusive touches. The curated package features exclusive MANUFAKTUR Cosmos Black Magno paint, front and rear fascias with black underguard, door and side sill trim in black and exclusive 20-inch AMG wheels in black. Striking accents also extend to the interior with illuminated door sills, Dark Shadow climate control air vent accents, sport seats finished in exclusive AMG Black MB-Tex/Microfiber upholstery with Crystal White A-band, center elements and white contrast stitching, exclusive Crystal White center armrest and Natural Fiber Zen trim.

A wide range of personalization options

A diverse range of exterior and interior colors is available, underscoring Mercedes-Benz’s commitment to exceptional design. New paints such as Liquid Crystal Green and Sky Blue Metallic expand the exterior color palette. Inside, new upholstery choices, including Beech Brown, have been added. The all-new GLA also features a variety of interior trim options, including natural grain wood, two aluminum finishes, innovative natural fiber and an anodized-look finish.

Universal: Built to adapt to real life and the many demands of everyday driving

The all-new GLA adapts seamlessly to different customer needs and lifestyles. It is designed for what really matters in life: maximum flexibility and practicality for everyday driving. Customers can choose between electric and hybrid powertrains with 48-volt technology. Whether it’s the daily commute to work, a spontaneous weekend trip or a long-awaited holiday – the all-new GLA is the perfect companion. It is equally at home on any road: agile and maneuverable in the city, dynamic on highways and country roads, and confident on dirt and gravel roads. State-of-the-art technology transforms every moment behind the wheel into an intuitive and comfortable experience.

“The new GLA is engineered to make advanced technology feel effortless. Powered by MB.OS and its AI-driven capabilities, it anticipates and supports to make everyday life noticeably easier. With a broad portfolio of all-electric and high-tech electrified combustion variants, up to 657 kilometers of range and 270 kilometers recharged in just 10 minutes, it redefines electric usability in its segment.”

Jörg Burzer, Member of the Board of Management, Mercedes-Benz Group AG,

Chief Technology Officer, Development & Procurement

The all-new electric GLA

With up to 657 kilometers of electric range (WLTP)1, the all-new electric GLA elevates everyday and long-distance driving to a new level. Up to 270 kilometers (WLTP)2 of range can be charged in as little as 10 minutes thanks to 800-volt technology. DC fast charging up to 320 kW is possible at 800-volt stations. A DC converter is also fitted standard to enable charging at 400-volt charging stations.

The 2028 Mercedes-Benz GLA portfolio features two all-electric models: the 268-hp GLA 250+ Electric and the 349-hp GLA 350 4MATIC Electric. The sporty top model sprints from 0 to 60 mph in 5.3 seconds. Both models are equipped with an NMC (nickel-manganese-cobalt) battery, which has an 85-kWh usable capacity.

Hybrid with 48-volt technology

The all-new GLA will also be available with hybrid powertrains in two outputs. The newly developed, electrified 1.5-liter four-cylinder turbo engine is designed to deliver both power and efficiency. The electric motor supplements the power of the combustion engine with an additional boost of 30 hp5. It is integrated directly into the new electrified eight-speed dual-clutch transmission (8F-eDCT) along with its components. This makes the entire system highly compact.

A new 48-volt battery with lithium-ion technology and a usable capacity of up to 1.3 kWh powers the electric motor. In city driving, under certain conditions, where less than 30 hp is required to keep the vehicle in motion6, the hybrid model can drive purely on electric power. Efficient electric coasting with the drivetrain disengaged is also possible at speeds up to 60 mph. In addition, recuperation in all eight gears is possible, with up to 25 kW of recuperation power.

TERRAIN mode and “Transparent Hood”

In addition to the ECO, COMFORT, SPORT and INDIVIDUAL drive programs, 4MATIC models feature the TERRAIN drive program. This mode automatically adjusts the characteristics of the drivetrain, steering and brakes for dirt and gravel roads. The “Transparent Hood” function, included with optional Digital Extra: MB.DRIVE PARKING ASSIST 3604, provides a virtual view of the area beneath the vehicle.

Intelligent navigation based on Google technology

The navigation experience in the all-new GLA is based on Google technology. The navigation solution, developed as part of the partnership between Google and Mercedes-Benz, is one of the first systems to integrate Google Cloud’s new Automotive AI Agent for in-vehicle conversational services with Google Maps. Customers can use the MBUX Virtual Assistant to search for charging stations as well as obtain information on the charging speed of stations.

Digital Extra: MBUX Navigation with Electric Intelligence4 plans the fastest and most convenient route, including charging stops when required, based on a variety of factors. It also responds dynamically to traffic jams or changes in driving style. Mercedes-Benz is also continuously refining the energy usage forecast. In the future, predicted wind conditions along the route will be considered even more precisely according to vehicle height.

MBUX Surround Navigation combines assistance and route guidance

With MBUX Surround Navigation, integrated visual interaction reaches a new dimension. Supported by the vehicle’s cameras and sensors, it displays a real‑time 3D representation of the vehicle and its surroundings on the driver display using 3D game engine graphics. Drivers benefit from improved situational awareness.

State-of-the-art MB.DRIVE assistance systems3

The all-new GLA is equipped standard with a number of driver assistance systems, including Digital Extra: Distance Assist DISTRONIC4, as well as eight cameras, five radar sensors, 12 ultrasonic sensors and a water-cooled high-performance control unit with sufficient power reserves for future functions and regular over-the-air updates. This high-performance computer can perform up to 254 tera operations per second (TOPS). Artificial intelligence processes all sensor data in real time to assess the current traffic situation.

The optional Digital Extra: MB.DRIVE PARKING ASSIST 3604 features the Digital Extra: 360 Camera4 and new and improved surround view display. It also includes Digital Extra: Rim Protection Warning4, which displays a top-view distance alert when maneuvering to help the driver avoid damage to the wheels.

Elevated: Interior experience and comfort at a new level

More space, more refinement, enhanced comfort and a new world of intuitive, personalized experiences

The all-new GLA offers more space for all occupants. The wheelbase has increased by 2.4 inches to 109.8 inches. The driver and front passenger benefit from an additional 0.3 inches of legroom. For rear passengers, legroom is increased by as much as 1.5 inches. The SUV’s roofline and standard panoramic glass roof create a generous sense of space and noticeably improve headroom. Maximum headroom for both the front and rear seats has increased by 0.9 inches.

The all-new GLA also offers plenty of cargo space. When folded down, the split-folding 40/20/40 rear seats create a nearly flat cargo floor.

“For many of our customers, the GLA is more than just a car, it is a trusted companion for everyday life. With the all-new GLA, we have focused on what matters most to them: a combination of sporty confidence with more space, elevated comfort and intuitive technologies that make everyday life easier. With a wide choice of powertrains and more opportunities for individualization than ever before, it fits seamlessly into modern lifestyles and, true to Mercedes-Benz, it delivers that unmistakable ‘Welcome home’ feeling every time you step inside.”

Mathias Geisen, Member of the Board of Management, Mercedes-Benz Group AG, Sales & Customer Experience

More light, more space: Standard panoramic roof

The standard fixed glass panoramic roof creates an exceptionally spacious and open feel. It is made from heat-insulating laminated safety glass with an infrared-reflective coating and an ultra-thin low-emissivity (LowE) coating. This helps reduce cabin temperatures in the summer. In winter weather, the LowE coating reduces interior heat loss by reflecting the interior heat back into the cabin.

With the optional SKY CONTROL, the glass surface of the panoramic roof can switch between transparent and opaque in 10 to 20 milliseconds. The glass roof is divided into seven segments, each of which can be controlled individually. This allows customers to choose how much sunlight they want to let into the interior, and in which area.

Interior design

The all-new GLA offers a new spatial experience in the segment. The previous sculptural design has been replaced by a clean, minimalist design concept. The focus is on a few striking, high-tech elements that structure and enhance the interior. A key highlight is the optional, floating MBUX Superscreen, which spans the entire width of the dashboard. A 10.25-inch driver display, 14-inch central display and 14-inch front passenger display are positioned beneath a large glass surface.

The circular climate control air vents at each end of the MBUX Superscreen also have a sporty high-tech look. The outer rings of the vents appear to float in front of a conical-shaped form. The center air vent replaces traditional vent louvers.

Another highlight is the door panels with a concave base that recedes visually, while floating-style door center panels with open storage make the interior appear lighter. The pull handle in the classic tubular design is minimalist in style yet still adds a powerful, sporty accent.

The sporty floating center console completes the new design concept. It blends elegantly beneath the optional MBUX Superscreen and is divided into two levels. The upper open surface features a large three-dimensional trim element, available in a variety of stunning finishes. The trim element integrates cupholders and a smartphone storage compartment with optional wireless charging.

Even more ergonomic and intuitive: New multifunction steering wheel with rocker and roller

The steering wheel is designed to be even more ergonomic and intuitive to operate. The control concept features a roller for volume control and a rocker for Digital Extra: Distance Assist DISTRONIC4. Capacitive control panels are also seamlessly integrated and feature tactile feedback.

Exceptionally intuitive and personalized: New MBUX control and display concept

The optional MBUX Superscreen is powered by state-of-the-art high-performance chips and real-time graphics from the Unity Game Engine. The new control and display concept is tailored to the individual preferences of customers. It follows the principle of reducing everything to the essentials. The enhanced MBUX Zero Layer on the central display shows the most relevant information, recently used apps4 and suggestions. In the app grid, customers can arrange and group apps into personalized folders, much like on a smartphone.

Attentive, intelligent and a great conversation partner: MBUX Virtual Assistant

The MBUX Virtual Assistant enables complex conversations, like one would have with a friend, and has short-term memory. AI from ChatGPT, Microsoft and Google unites the collective knowledge of the internet, enabling the intelligent assistant to seamlessly access different sources of information within the same conversation and retain context. With this unique “multi-agent approach,” the MBUX Virtual Assistant revolutionizes the relationship between the vehicle and the driver – transforming it into a natural, intuitive interaction. The virtual assistant appears as a “living” avatar on the MBUX Zero Layer.

Individual entertainment for the front passenger

With the optional MBUX Superscreen, the all-new GLA offers the front passenger their own 14-inch display for personalized entertainment. The growing portfolio of apps7 elevates in-car entertainment with video streaming platforms like Disney+ and Sony RIDEVU, as well as streaming audio apps and video conferencing apps.

Personalized ambient lighting with dynamic effects

Optional ambient lighting visually enhances the interior. It also emphasizes the floating design of the three central interior elements: the center console, door center panels and optional MBUX Superscreen. With 64 colors, 10 color schemes, 20 brightness levels and three brightness zones, customers can personalize the lighting atmosphere of the cabin.

In addition, high-resolution, atmospheric ambient styles can be selected as mood-enhancing background motifs for the displays. The color scheme of the driver display, controls and ambient lighting is coordinated accordingly. Together with the high-quality materials and stunning details, the lighting and graphic designs create an atmosphere that appeals to the senses and takes the familiar “Welcome home” feeling to a new level.

Music enjoyment with greater spatiality and depth: Burmester® 3D Surround Sound System

The new optional Burmester® 3D Surround Sound System with Dolby Atmos7 delivers an impressive multidimensional music experience. The system features four additional speakers – 16 speakers in total – and a powerful 850-watt amplifier. For the first time in the GLA, the covers for the tweeters and mid-range speakers in the front doors are finished in silver chrome.

The overall sound of the Burmester® 3D Surround Sound System has been further optimized. A new algorithm ensures significantly greater spatiality and depth. Customers can adjust the spatiality across 10 levels (the “3D Sound” menu). Another new feature allows the music to be directed only to the first or second row of seats (the “Sound Zone” setting). This means front occupants can enjoy the full sound when the rear seats are empty. In addition, the sound can be directed to the rear passengers if the driver prefers a quieter environment. The sound focus can also be specifically optimized for the driver’s seat or both rows of seats (the “Focus” setting). The new Auto Selection feature detects the occupants seated in the vehicle and adjusts the sound focus accordingly. Auto Selection is automatically activated in default mode.

Exceptionally quiet interior for a relaxed driving experience

A highly rigid body structure complemented by a wide range of measures is designed to ensure high levels of NVH refinement in the all-new GLA. These include extensive sound insulation from the front to the rear, decoupling elastomer mounts between the chassis and body, double decoupling of the electric motor from the body and enclosures for the electric drive in the GLA Electric.

Aerodynamics further contribute to the high level of acoustic comfort. The all-new GLA is more aerodynamic than its predecessor. Thanks to its streamlined silhouette and extensive aerodynamic detailing, the new SUV achieves a drag coefficient of 0.26. The excellent aerodynamics reduce wind noise and also help maximize electric range.

Mercedes-Benz Anniversary Year “140 Years of Innovation”

Since Carl Benz filed the patent for the first automobile 140 years ago and Gottlieb Daimler built his motorized carriage shortly afterward, Mercedes-Benz has dedicated itself to constant innovation and to creating the world’s most desirable cars for customers. This ambition has driven every innovation – from the world’s first automobile in 1886 to the biggest product launch program in the company’s history that is currently underway. With its passion for performance and pioneering power, excellence and an unwavering commitment to customer service, the brand has consistently shaped the future of mobility. The result goes well beyond engineering achievement – it creates the unmistakable feeling that leads through everything Mercedes-Benz does: Welcome home.

Mercedes-Benz is celebrating 140 years of innovation: Three new S-Class sedans went on a transcontinental journey to 140 locations worldwide as part of the “140 Years. 140 Places” tour. Each place highlighted the brand’s technology, heritage, pioneering spirit and worldwide presence. Along the way, customers, fans and colleagues got to join in the celebrations right up to its grand ‘Homecoming’ finale at the Mercedes-Benz Museum. Highlights of the tour can be found on our “140 Years of Innovation | Mercedes-Benz Media” special.

About Mercedes-Benz USA

Mercedes-Benz USA (MBUSA), headquartered in Atlanta, is responsible for the distribution, marketing and customer service for all Mercedes-Benz products in the United States. MBUSA offers drivers the most diverse lineup in the luxury segment with 18 model lines ranging from the sporty GLA SUV to the flagship S-Class and the dynamic all-electric vehicles from Mercedes-Benz. MBUSA is also responsible for Mercedes-Benz Vans in the U.S. More information on MBUSA and its products can be found at www.mbusa.com and www.mbvans.com. To learn more about all Mercedes-Benz entities in North America, visit group.mercedes-benz.com/northamerica.

On Nov. 18, 2026, the New York Department of Public Service (DPS) Staff released its white paper in Case 26-E-0335, the Nuclear Reliability Backbone proceeding of the Public Service Commission (Commission). The paper sets out Staff’s recommendations on how New York should pursue a cost-effective path to new, advanced nuclear generation. It builds on the stakeholder comments and an Oct. 5, 2026, technical conference that DPS Staff convened under the Commission’s June 11, 2026, order.

Background: New York’s 8.4 GW Nuclear Reliability Backbone and NYPA’s 1 GW Project

In her 2026 State of the State address, Gov. Kathy Hochul called for a Nuclear Reliability Backbone and directed the Commission to facilitate a cost-effective pathway to 4 GW of new advanced nuclear energy. That followed her June 2025 directive to the New York Power Authority (NYPA) to develop and construct a separate advanced nuclear plant of at least 1 GW in upstate New York. Together, the two initiatives total 5 GW of new nuclear power, which, combined with the existing 3.4 GW fleet, would form an 8.4 GW “backbone” of clean, reliable, firm, 24×7, 365 energy, along with the transmission needed to deliver it.

According to the white paper, when the State’s grid model was allowed to include new nuclear power, it chose 5 GW. That reduced the need ro construct 20 GW of additional renewable energy and 3 GW of new transmission while still allowing the State to meet its climate change goals. The 2025 State Energy Plan estimated that by including nuclear, the benefits of the energy system would outweigh its costs by $28–$31 billion by 2040, while the 2026 NY Advanced Nuclear Policy Options Paper estimated the public cost of supporting 5 GW of new nuclear at roughly $15.4 to $23.9 billion over the first 25 years of operation.

While the white paper describes large light-water reactors as the most mature technology option, it still notes a high level of project risks. The paper also notes that while U.S. Department of Energy debt may cover up to 80% of the capital cost of initial projects, it would still leave an equity requirement of at least 20%, or roughly $2 billion for a GW-scale project.

NYPA is advancing its 1 GW project on a parallel track. On Nov. 12, 2026, NYPA announced that it had qualified 10 developers from 21 responses to its request for qualifications: six for both large-scale and small modular reactors, and four for small modular reactors only. Staff expects NYPA’s process to inform the design of the State’s pre-qualification process.

DPS Staff’s Five Recommendations: Revenue Support, Pre-Qualification, and Procurement for Advanced Nuclear

DPS Staff makes five recommendations. It asks the Commission to (1) adopt the 8.4 GW Nuclear Reliability Backbone, with a target of 5 GW of new advanced nuclear and determine that State support is justified. It also asks the Commission to direct DPS and the New York State Energy Research and Development Authority (NYSERDA) to (2) develop a revenue support mechanism, (3) create an eligibility and pre-qualification process, (4) establish a competitive open-book negotiation process, and (5) develop a Procurement Framework and file an Implementation Plan for the Commission’s consideration.

Staff states that no single mechanism would address all barriers to deployment and that ratepayers should not bear the full cost of support. It proposes revenue support that pays out only once a project is operating, alongside State equity, limited State sharing of cost-overrun risk, and support before a final investment decision. Staff does not consider a sole State equity stake viable and is silent on the question of utility ownership.

For procurement, Staff proposes pre-qualification followed by competitive open-book negotiations rather than a traditional request for proposals. Its proposed eligibility standards cover new advanced nuclear only, projects of at least 250 MW, and in-state projects in New York Independent System Operator (NYISO) Zones A-F. Staff considers it premature to set a specific pipeline or sequencing strategy.

Next Steps for Advanced Nuclear in New York: Commission Action and NYSERDA’s Master Plan

The white paper is a Staff recommendation that is now subject to stakeholder feedback. If the Commission proceeds, DPS and NYSERDA would develop an Implementation Plan for the Commission to approve, and the pre-qualification process would open after the Commission acts.

Separately, NYSERDA and DPS co-authored the State’s Advanced Nuclear Master Plan, which Gov. Hochul announced on Nov. 18. The 30-point plan draws on 12 studies and addresses commercial viability, siting, community partnerships, State regulatory processes, workforce readiness, and supply chain capacity. NYSERDA will host a public webinar on the Master Plan on Jan. 13.

*Special thanks to Legislative Specialist Olivia Sheffer for contributing to this blog post.

Chapter 1. Introduction to Hybrid Electric Vehicles for Sustainable Transport: Standardization, Challenges and Future Prospects

Hemant Thakur, Gajendra Singh, Atul Dhar

Abstract

The transportation sector is a major contributor to global greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions. Hybrid electric vehicles (HEVs) offer a promising and scalable pathway towards decarbonising the transportation sector and achieving emission reduction targets. However, fully realising their emission reduction potential requires an integrated approach encompassing engine design and optimisation, driving conditions, vehicle operating strategies, and the optimisation of key vehicle characteristics. It also necessitates the development of appropriate emission standards and supportive policy frameworks tailored to hybrid powertrain technologies. This chapter introduces the scope and organisation of the book, outlining its coverage of plug-in hybrid electric vehicles (PHEVs), strong hybrid electric vehicles, the role of engine design and optimisation, and the influence of alternative fuels on HEV performance and emissions. By presenting these interconnected themes, the chapter establishes the foundation for a comprehensive understanding of the technological, operational, and policy dimensions of harnessing the potential of HEVs for sustainable and low-emission transportation.

Dive into the core of hybrid electric vehicle (HEV) technology with this chapter, which dissects the architecture and operational principles of these innovative vehicles. You’ll explore the rationale behind hybridization, driven by stringent emissions regulations and global sustainability goals, and gain insights into the key subsystems that make HEVs tick—from internal combustion engines and electric traction motors to high-voltage battery systems and advanced control units. The chapter also examines the critical role of energy management strategies in optimizing fuel efficiency and reducing emissions, while highlighting the impact of vehicle design and component sizing on overall performance. Beyond technical details, it provides a detailed overview of global emission standards and policy frameworks, offering a clear picture of how HEVs are positioned within the broader context of sustainable transport. Whether you're interested in the latest advancements in plug-in hybrid technology, the future of alternative fuels, or the regulatory landscape shaping HEV manufacturing, this chapter delivers a structured and insightful exploration of the challenges and opportunities in hybrid mobility.

Chsapter 2. Optimization Strategies for Major Hybrid Electric Vehicle Powertrain Architectures

Prashant Saini, Julian D. Osorio

Abstract

Hybrid electric vehicles (HEVs) combine internal combustion engines with electric propulsion systems to improve fuel economy, reduce emissions, recover braking energy and provide flexible operation under varying driving conditions. This chapter reviews the principal HEV powertrain architectures and the optimization strategies used to improve their design and operation. The optimization approaches considered include powertrain-topology selection, component-sizing and dynamic-parameter matching, multi-objective system optimization, rule-based and fuzzy-logic control, dynamic programming, model-predictive control, metaheuristic methods and data-driven energy-management strategies. The major series, parallel and series–parallel or power-split architectures are compared in terms of power-flow pathways, component requirements, energy-conversion losses, control complexity, operating flexibility and typical applications. Series architectures provide mechanically simple axle-side operation and are particularly suitable for urban and stop-and-go duty cycles, although repeated mechanical–electrical energy conversion can reduce efficiency during sustained high-speed operation. Parallel architectures provide a direct mechanical path from the engine to the wheels and are generally advantageous during steady-speed and highway driving, but require coordinated torque blending and drivetrain control. Chapter 10. Numerical Modelling of Hybrid Electric Vehicles for Improvement Scope in the Emission Norms

Gaurav Kumar, Hemant Thakur, Atul Dhar, Gajendra Singh

Abstract

The testing standards for hybrid electric vehicles (HEVs) are still in development, despite their ever-growing demand, especially in India, given the current Automotive Testing Standards (AIS). In the current system, HEVs are tested similarly to conventional vehicles (CVs) using standard cycles such as WHSC, WHTC, WLTC, IDC and real-time driving emission (RDE). Due to its complexity, RDE is not included in many test standards despite its best results. Although the HEVs run on a battery for most of their operation, the standards do not specify any power-sharing strategy between the battery and the ICE. The battery’s charge status and hybridisation (type and amount) are not being considered during testing. Consequently, significant discrepancies were observed in their testing and type approval, particularly regarding fuel consumption and real-time emissions. The present study simulated five types of HEVs using the Simulink powertrain model under different driving conditions (NEDC, WLTC and JC 08) and at different initial battery state of charge (SOC) levels. The maximum reductions in fuel consumption for JC 08 and NEDC were 56.73% and 55.47%, respectively, for the full-hybrid vehicle compared with the conventional vehicle. The maximum fuel-saving of 38% was observed for a full-hybrid vehicle under the WLTP drive cycle. The minimum HC reduction was 24.14% compared to a conventional vehicle under the WLTP drive cycle for a full-hybrid vehicle. The minimum CO emissions reduction was observed for a full-hybrid vehicle under the WLTP drive cycle. The fuel consumption was increased by 52.84% at 50% initial SOC compared to 80% SOC for a full-hybrid electric vehicle. Similarly, HC and CO emissions increased by 57% and 46.5%, respectively, for a full-hybrid electric vehicle. However, NOX emissions increased by 98% at 50% initial SOC compared to 80% initial SOC. The battery energy used at 50% initial SOC was reduced by 34% in a full-hybrid vehicle. Finally, the chapter summarised that considering HEV operating variables leads to wide discrepancies in their emissions and performance, as well as in the motor and engine energy contributions. The focus is kept on quantitatively justifying the need to develop HEV-specific regulations, which should include the real drive cycle (RDC) and RDE limits, hybridisation and vehicle configuration, the status of the battery (charge and power split) and the impact of the transmission unit.

The chapter introduces a numerical modelling approach using Simulink to simulate HEV performance across different drive cycles, including the New European Driving Cycle (NEDC), Worldwide Harmonised Light Vehicle Test Cycle (WLTC), and Japanese JC08 cycle. text:
U.S. data center developers expanding AI infrastructure are increasing construction of their own natural gas-fired power plants to address power shortages. The approach can shorten the time needed to connect to the grid, but it is also raising concerns it could increase greenhouse gas emissions and drive up electricity bills.

MIT Technology Review reported on Nov. 24 that energy market research firm Cleanview counted more than 100 on-site fossil-fuel power projects at U.S. data centers as of October this year, with total installed capacity exceeding 115 gigawatts (GW). That is more than twice California's peak power demand.

Cleanview's latest tally put the number of projects at 120, with total installed capacity rising to 129 GW. Actual operating capacity as of October was only 4.9 GW, while 15.8 GW was under construction, leaving it uncertain whether all projects will be realised.

The trend is being driven by delays in grid connections. For data centers that consume large amounts of electricity, it can take up to 10 years to connect to the grid because of constraints in expanding infrastructure such as transmission lines and transformers. Developers are therefore adopting behind-the-meter (BTM) generation, producing power directly on site even at higher cost.

A key issue is that reliance on fossil fuels could deepen. BloombergNEF (BNEF) estimated planned global construction of data center on-site fossil-fuel plants at 181 GW, with more than 90 percent concentrated in the United States.

BNEF estimated that if all U.S. plans are carried out, annual greenhouse gas emissions would reach 345 million tonnes in carbon dioxide equivalent terms. That would be 152 million tonnes more than supplying power to the same data centers through the U.S. grid.

The economic burden is also significant. The Rocky Mountain Institute (RMI) estimated that grid usage costs for large U.S. power consumers range from $55 to $115 per megawatt hour (MWh), compared with estimated costs of $100 to $165 for self-generated fossil-fuel power.

Experts said expanding self-generation at data centers could increase natural gas demand and lift fuel prices, adding to electricity bill burdens for ordinary consumers. With rapid growth in the AI industry, securing stable power supplies while cutting carbon is emerging as a key task.

text:
Australia has the natural resources and know-how to create a thriving battery manufacturing industry but is missing opportunities by exporting critical minerals rather than turning them into high-value products.

Scientists from the CSIRO issued the warning at an event on Tuesday, also recommending more international partnerships and a greater focus on manufacturing individual components rather than trying to make entire batteries.

The call comes as Australians embrace battery technology, with more than 600,000 home batteries installed under a federal scheme since July 2025 and rapid electric vehicle sales since March.

Speaking at an event called Australia’s Battery Opportunity, CSIRO mineral resources principal research scientist Joanne Loh said the nation had enviable access to valuable raw materials.

“We have all the minerals needed for batteries, specifically lithium-ion batteries – we’re the number one producer in terms of lithium… we have nickel, cobalt, manganese, aluminium, copper, graphite, you name it,” she said.“However, we export all of these as raw materials overseas so even though we might have it, we’re actually sending it overseas for processing, then importing them back as batteries.”

The nation also shredded batteries at the end of their lives and exported the materials, Dr Loh said, rather than using them.

Australia had also stopped manufacturing elements that could be used in batteries, such as aluminium foil, CSIRO senior research engineer Geoff de Looze said.

The nation could re-establish that facility, he said, and target the local production of key components like aluminium casings and copper foil.

“We do have some gaps in Australia’s capability so when we look at them we need to rank them and work out which ones we can take on and which ones we want to leave alone,” de Looze said.

“Any of the manufactured parts going into batteries, Australia can take on.”

A CSIRO report released early in November found Australia could use its expertise in manufacturing aluminium aerosol cans to produce battery casings, for example, or manufacture copper foil from scrap wire.

Identifying gaps in the global battery supply chain could allow Australian companies to partner with larger manufacturing firms from the region, CSIRO senior principal research scientist Adam Best said, rather than competing with an established industry.

“We need to work closely with our partners in Asia, Pacific, North America, Europe, to find where we fit in this middle part such that we can do… that manufacturing, that value-adding, to capture more value from our resources,” he said.

“Then Australia does have a brighter future that can lead to a future with energy security,” he said.

Carol Leonnig’s disturbing reporting on the Trump administration’s retreat from environmental enforcement brings me back to a warning I made in 2024.

During an interview with Angela Greene on her Atlanta radio show, I warned about the consequences of my uncle’s plans to roll back environmental protections, particularly for underserved communities.

My cousins are accomplished fly fisherman. They will always be able to find pristine rivers and streams.

But what about families living near polluted waterways, industrial waste sites and factories contaminating the air their children breathe. They simply cannot pack up and leave.

And now look at Iowa.

The Army plans to detonate nearly five tons of unstable, lead-based explosives, potentially spreading toxic lead particles into surrounding communities. The Army insists it is necessary for safety. Environmental groups are challenging the decision and demanding answers about alternatives and public protections.

These are different situations, but they raise a common question: Who bears the environmental risks, and who gets a meaningful say.

The wealthy can often escape pollution. Working families frequently cannot.

Environmental protections are not bureaucratic inconveniences. They are safeguards for people who cannot afford to protect themselves.

When those protections fail, those with the least often pay the highest price.

description:
The United States has imposed tariffs of up to 127.5% on Chinese-made EVs, effectively blocking Chinese vehicles from entering its market.
The policy has helped reduce the share of Chinese-made EVs among new vehicles sold in France.
An active response is also urgently needed in South Korea, where sales of Chinese-made EVs are growing.
The key issue is whether EVs will be included in a domestic production tax credit intended to maintain the domestic EV supply chain.
If support for domestic vehicle production is reduced, small and midsize parts suppliers will inevitably take a direct hit.
text:
Countries around the world are deploying a range of policy tools to counter Chinese-made electric vehicles as they expand globally. Some are imposing tariffs on the grounds that the vehicles benefit from Chinese government subsidies, while others are overhauling their purchase subsidy systems to strongly protect their domestic industries.

South Korea, by contrast, faces the risk of ceding its market to the Chinese EV offensive without being able to respond, as the government is reluctant to offer tax credits for EVs produced and sold domestically.

According to industry sources on November 25, the United States, the European Union (EU), India and other markets are strengthening protectionist measures to prevent an influx of Chinese-made EVs.

The United States has imposed tariffs of up to 127.5% on Chinese-made EVs, effectively blocking Chinese vehicles from entering its market.

It has also tightened regulations on connected cars, a sector critical to future mobility competitiveness, in the name of national security and supply chain protection. Starting with 2027 model-year vehicles, imports and sales in the United States will be completely banned for vehicles equipped with connectivity or autonomous driving software developed by Chinese companies.

India also imposes a basic tariff of at least 70% on imported automobiles, applying a 15% tariff as an exception only when companies meet local investment requirements.

The EU conducted an anti-subsidy investigation into Chinese-made EVs and is imposing tariffs of up to 45.3%. The system adds countervailing duties to the basic 10% tariff, with the additional amount determined by the scale of Chinese government subsidies received. Companies that did not cooperate with the investigation, including SAIC Motor, face tariffs of 45.3%; BYD is subject to a 27.0% tariff, and Geely a 28.8% tariff.

France, in particular, tightened the eligibility requirements for its EV purchase subsidy, the "Bonus Écologique," in December 2023. The policy has helped reduce the share of Chinese-made EVs among new vehicles sold in France. The revised criteria added emissions generated before a vehicle is driven, including those from its production and transportation, excluding vehicles such as the Tesla Model 3 produced in China from eligibility for subsidies.

As a result, according to global market research firm Benchmark Mineral Intelligence (BMI), the share of Chinese-made EVs among new vehicles sold in France fell by 18.0 percentage points in just two years, from 31.4% in 2023 to 16.4% in 2024 and 13.4% in 2025.

Over the same period, new vehicle sales rose 9.6%, from 298,522 in 2023 to 327,234 in 2025, indicating that France succeeded in curbing Chinese-made EVs.

An active response is also urgently needed in South Korea, where sales of Chinese-made EVs are growing. The government is set to announce measures to strengthen EV competitiveness on November 27. The key issue is whether EVs will be included in a domestic production tax credit intended to maintain the domestic EV supply chain.

However, discussions at the National Assembly's Finance and Economy Planning Committee tax subcommittee the previous day failed to produce an agreement on EV tax credits. The government is reportedly concerned that supporting automakers could escalate into a trade issue.

If support for domestic vehicle production is reduced, small and midsize parts suppliers will inevitably take a direct hit. As of 2024, the domestic automotive industry accounted for 14.1% of total shipments from South Korea's manufacturing sector. It plays an important role in the domestic economy, generating about 1.54 million direct and indirect jobs across the broader industry, including vehicle and parts manufacturing, sales, maintenance and logistics.

"A decline in vehicle production immediately leads to fewer parts orders, directly affecting capacity utilization and employment at small and midsize suppliers," said the head of an automotive parts company. "Investment costs are also arising during the transition to electrification, so simply maintaining production has become the biggest challenge on the ground."

title: Midterm wins you may have missed - Vital Signs
description:
The midterm elections on November 3 transformed the political landscape in Washington.
The election results brought a sea change to state level politics across the United States.
Here are just a few of the key state level midterm wins that will help accelerate climate progress across the country.
The election results create opportunities for bipartisan, practical solutions to the state’s water and energy challenges.
The election results create significant new opportunities to shape Texas's energy agenda through the Governor's office, a Democratic-led House, and executive and regulatory appointments.
text:
The midterm elections on November 3 transformed the political landscape in Washington. But it’s not just the nation’s capital that was radically remodeled. The election results brought a sea change to state level politics across the United States.

“In key ballot measures and local races across the nation, voters sent an unmistakable message,” says Dawn Shirreffs, Florida state director at the climate-focused nonprofit Environmental Defense Fund. “They reject false choices that pit affordability against the health of their communities. They want to protect their families, clean up local air and water, and keep money in their pockets. We need to provide clear and tangible climate solutions that align with these priorities.”

While progress in Washington may still be stymied by an administration determined to promote fossil fuels, it is full steam ahead for climate action in an ever-growing number of states.

Here are just a few of the key state level midterm wins that will help accelerate climate progress across the country.

New state leadership

In states from the Northeast to the Midwest and the Southwest, voters helped flip control of governorships and state legislatures in favor of candidates offering solutions for soaring energy prices and unchecked pollution.

In Arizona, where unregulated groundwater extraction in rural areas is endangering property owners and community futures, the Colorado River is in crisis, and energy demand and costs are increasing rapidly, voters chose to reelect strong environmental champions in Governor Katie Hobbs and Attorney General Kris Mayes and for new, pro-environment leadership in both the state House and Senate. The election results create opportunities for bipartisan, practical solutions to the state’s water and energy challenges.

“Arizona voters made clear they want a new approach,” says Kevin Moran, Arizona state director at EDF. “The logjam blocking environmental policy, decades in the making, is starting to break. The door is now open to bold action on groundwater protections, promoting clean energy, data center safeguards and restoring environmental protections.”

Arizona residents win long-sought water protections

In Pennsylvania, new, unified state government under Governor Josh Shapiro also promises to end years of obstruction and inaction on key energy and environment issues.

“Pennsylvania voters sent a clear message calling for change and placing their hopes in a new governing coalition to work together and deliver results for the Commonwealth,” says Peter Daigle, who helps lead EDF’s legislative efforts in Pennsylvania. “As Pennsylvania’s energy needs continue to grow, there is an important opportunity to expand clean energy, protect families from rising electricity costs and pollution associated with data center development, and strengthen methane safeguards to address increasing pressures on the energy system.”

The November 3 election also fundamentally reshaped Texas politics for the next few years, as voters put Democrats into every statewide office for the first time in three decades. The election results create significant new opportunities to shape Texas's energy agenda through the Governor's office, a Democratic-led House, and executive and regulatory appointments.

“We can now move past the misguided fights against Texas's abundant wind and solar resources that help keep electricity clean and affordable for all customers,” says Colin Leyden, Texas state director at EDF. “Texans made clear that they expect their government to put the health, safety and well-being of Texas families first. This marks a new chapter for the state and an opportunity to lower energy costs, invest in disaster response and prevention, give communities sensible safeguards for data center development and balance economic development with protecting our natural resources.”

“What I see across the map is proof that voters are frustrated with high costs and corporate pollution and willing to embrace practical solutions that address rising utility bills, provide clean energy, clean air, clean water and lower costs,” says Shirreffs.

text:
Murat Kurum, the Turkish environment minister and president of the 2026 U.N. Conference of the Parties to the U.N. Framework Convention on Climate Change had proposed an agreement that included increasing the global share of final energy demand—the energy available to end users—met by electricity to 35% by 2035, from about 20-23% today; reducing the operational intensity of building stock by 25% relative to 2020 levels; tripling financing for adaptation and other goals intended to reduce climate change.

By the final scheduled day of the conference, more than 90 countries had agreed to back the 2035 electrification pledge, which also had support from many business groups at the summit. But negotiators were split on including references to transitioning away from fossil fuels and on the use of carbon capture and storage. Talks continued into the weekend, making it the longest COP summit to date, but by Nov. 22, officials admitted they had reached a stalemate.

“We did everything we could,” Kurum said.

Ani Dasgupta, president and CEO of the World Resources Institute, a nature- and climate-focused research nonprofit, called the outcome “a failure of political leadership, not a failure of the Paris agreement” which established the international goal of limiting climate change to a 1.5° C warming threshold, to prevent the worst of the impacts from climate change.

The draft COP31 pact had included language noting that peak global warming is now expected to exceed the 1.5° C threshold.

“At a time when the science could not be clearer, it is indefensible that countries could not agree on even mentioning fossil fuels, the primary driver of climate change,” Dasgupta said in a written statement. “The science has long settled this question—it's time for the politics to catch up.”

The lack of agreement means that even the popular 2035 electrification goal is not an official outcome of the summit, although countries that backed the goal can still work toward it.

Congressional Involvement

The U.S. would not have been party to the agreement since it did not send an official delegation for the second consecutive year. America also withdrew from the Paris agreement for the second time under the Trump administration, sandwiched between a reinstatement by the Biden administration between the current president's two terms. However, 18 members of Congress—all Democrats—attended COP31 and indicated they plan to back legislation focused on energy and climate reform.

“We feel a moral obligation, also a business obligation, an affordability obligation to our people to begin to get back on track … towards cleaner, cheaper energy, cutting costs and cutting pollution, Rep. Kathy Castor (D-Fla.) said during a press conference. “That is our goal.”

Democrats at the summit said they will back infrastructure development to support expanded power grid and load flexibility as well as technology to improve grid efficiency and resilience. They also aim to create an environment that is attractive for manufacturing investment and local economic development. Lawmakers also intend to provide low-cost finance to spur private investment in clean energy, grid modernization and innovation and deployment of “clean” technology.

Even data centers, which have been the subject of controversy in many communities, are included, said Rep. Mike Levin (D-Calif.), but the aim is to keep the costs of their development from impacting ratepayers, and to ensure that they are powered by clean energy.

Since Democrats won a majority of the House and Senate in the U.S. midterm elections on Nov, 3, Rep. Jared Huffman (D-Calif.) said he expects Congress to send an official delegation to the next COP summit, to be held next November in Ethiopia.

“With a new Congress on the horizon, our members will work with the knowledge that climate action and economic prosperity go hand in hand,” he said. “The next Congress will lead with our values, which certainly includes a commitment to science and a future-focused healthy livable planet.”

text:
The U.S. Senate passed a bipartisan bill seeking to expedite and cheapen energy production and infrastructure development, despite national concerns from environmental groups and tribal nations.

The Senate voted 62-33 in favor of the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act of 2026 on Thursday, handing the bill to the House of Representatives. Colorado’s Democratic senators were split on the measure, with Sen. John Hickenlooper voting in favor and Sen. Michael Bennet voting against.

BAAJA reforms federal permitting processes by removing permit requirements for onshore oil and gas drilling on nonfederal land; accelerating energy projects; and making it easier for the federal government to greenlight interstate electricity transmission projects, among other initiatives, according to a congressional summary.

All of that has the goal of removing red tape for building out energy infrastructure, proponents argue, as well as potentially accelerating the country’s transition to renewable energy sources.

But since the bill was introduced on Sept. 30, several clauses have prompted public pushback.

The bill would severely limit future administrations and Congresses from canceling or correcting drilling and mining projects on public land. It would also impact tribal consultation regarding energy projects on shared lands.

The Wilderness Society, a Washington, D.C.-based nonprofit public lands advocacy group, argues the bill would broadly “expand industry access to public lands without adequate safeguards.”

“It would effectively hand over control of our public lands to oil and gas drilling, mining, AI data centers,” said Jim Ramey, the Wilderness Society’s Colorado state director. “Once permits are issued, it will be incredibly difficult, if not impossible, to undo those.”

“Even if they’re issued illegally, even if new science comes to light, even if a community is vehemently opposed to whatever that project might be,” Ramey added.

While the bill paves the way for consumer price protections from high-demand projects like data centers, it limits the National Environmental Policy Act, expedites environmental reviews and narrows the scope of review for water quality certifications under the Clean Water Act.

Ramey said he’s concerned to see such a sweeping law introduced and advanced so rapidly during a lame-duck session of Congress, two months before Democrats take control of both the Senate and House of Representatives. Despite public concerns being voiced, the Senate passed the bill without time to consider amendments.

The legislation could have direct impacts on Pitkin and Garfield counties, which are roughly 85% and 60% public land, respectively. About 5,000 acres of Garfield County’s Roan Plateau is planned to be leased for oil and gas drilling in December, and communities in the Roaring Fork region have for decades fought off repeated drilling initiatives in the Thompson Divide, to great success.

If President Donald Trump were to sign the bill into law, prospective permits like those on the Roan Plateau would be nearly impossible to amend or cancel in the future, Ramey said. In the past 20 years, federal courts and the government have changed and halted drilling permits to preserve both areas — decisions that would likely not happen under the permitting bill.

“Once these places are lost, once they’re developed, they’re often lost forever,” Ramey said.

Tribal opposition

Tribal governments have opposed the bill, specifically for its limitations on national historic preservation law. They argue these cut them out of review processes.

Ira Matt, executive director of the National Association of Tribal Historic Preservation Officers, said in a statement that the bill “ignores the real causes of permitting delays and weakens requirements for federal agencies to consult with Tribal Nations and consider how projects could harm places of historic, cultural, or spiritual importance to us.”

Other organizations like the Native American Rights Fund have opposed the bill over concern that it would allow federal agencies to decide whether to consult Tribes by letting the agencies determine on their own if a project has “adverse effect” on a sacred cultural site.

“We should have helped shape this legislation. Instead, lawmakers developed a bill changing our protections without meaningful government-to-government consultation,” said Harry Antonio Jr., governor and chief executive officer of the Pueblo of Laguna in New Mexico.

Antonio Jr. spoke at a Nov. 9 rally in Washington, D.C., against the bill.

Colorado senators defend decision

In a statement, Sen. Bennet said he opposed the legislation in part because it insufficiently ensured Tribal governments’ voice in land use decisions. He said it also “fundamentally overhauls” how the government engages with local communities about projects as they move through the permitting process.

Bennet added that, while the electric grid needs improvement and new energy sources, “permitting reform is complex, and the details matter.”

“I am concerned that not all perspectives were sufficiently heard during the drafting of this far-reaching piece of legislation,” Bennet’s statement read.

Hickenlooper, who for years has called for reforming what he said is “all too often a decades-long timeline to build new transmission lines and clean energy projects,” defended his support for the bill.

“Where we’ve landed isn’t perfection,” Hickenlooper said in a statement. “But it is progress toward delivering on our promise to bring down prices, hold Big Tech accountable, and stop the Trump administration’s attacks on clean energy. Our work with Tribal Nations and environmental groups doesn’t end with today’s vote. We’ll keep pushing to address their concerns.”

His statement cited an analysis that found the bill would create up to 105,600 trades and manufacturing jobs over the next 15 years and require data centers to pay an estimated $55 billion in increased energy costs over the next decade. According to the study, the bill could also nearly double the amount of solar and wind that can connect to the grid and save $19 billion in residential electricity bills over the next 14 years.

The bill will next go through the House of Representatives, which has voting days scheduled through Dec. 17. After that, House leaders will have to extend the session or call lawmakers back into session to pass the bill before the new Congress takes over on Jan. 3.

Until then, the permitting bill will compete for floor time against year-end deadlines, including a funding resolution to keep the government open through the holidays.

description:
The government has amended the End-of-Life Vehicles Rules, 2025, to clarify that the provision governing unfulfilled extended producer responsibility (EPR) obligations will apply only when a vehicle producer permanently ceases operations.
How the EPR framework works The End-of-Life Vehicles Rules, which came into force on April 1, 2025, require automakers to meet annual scrapping targets linked to vehicles introduced into the market 15 to 20 years earlier.
Producers can meet these obligations by purchasing EPR certificates from registered vehicle scrapping facilities through a centralised portal.

text:
The government has amended the End-of-Life Vehicles Rules, 2025, to clarify that the provision governing unfulfilled extended producer responsibility (EPR) obligations will apply only when a vehicle producer permanently ceases operations.

The Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change notified the amendments on November 20, following concerns from automobile manufacturers over the potential financial implications of the original framework. Under the revised Rule 4(6), the provision will not apply to producers that continue operations. In the event of permanent closure, a producer must submit details of vehicles introduced into the market over the preceding 15 years for transport vehicles and 20 years for non-transport vehicles.

The Central Board will then determine and communicate the producer's outstanding EPR obligations as on the date of cessation, in accordance with the applicable provisions.Industry concerns over provisioning Automobile manufacturers had flagged that the original rules, when read alongside accounting standard Ind AS 37, could lead to significant provisions in financial statements for the future cost of meeting vehicle scrapping obligations.

Industry estimates had pointed to a potential one-time gross provisioning requirement running into tens of thousands of crores under the earlier interpretation. Executives had also warned that the impact could become more pronounced once environmental compensation rates for non-compliance were notified.

The amendment provides clarity on the application of Rule 4(6), although it does not remove the broader EPR requirements applicable to vehicle producers.

How the EPR framework works The End-of-Life Vehicles Rules, which came into force on April 1, 2025, require automakers to meet annual scrapping targets linked to vehicles introduced into the market 15 to 20 years earlier. Producers can meet these obligations by purchasing EPR certificates from registered vehicle scrapping facilities through a centralised portal. The certificates are generated based on the quantity of steel recovered from scrapped vehicles, allowing manufacturers to fulfil their obligations without directly undertaking scrapping operations.

The amendment also removes a reference to other automobile-sector steel scrap materials processed at registered vehicle scrapping facilities from Rule 9(2).

text:
Updated November 24, 2026 at 12:09 PM EST

KOLWEZI, Democratic Republic of Congo — In a small cinderblock home in the scrub beside a Chinese-owned copper and cobalt mine in Kolwezi, a mother shares a story of devastating loss.

She believes pollution from the neighboring mine is responsible for her family's suffering.

She has lost three children. Two died at birth. A third suffered repeated nosebleeds before dying. One of her two surviving children has stunted growth.

Now she and 26 other residents are taking the company to court in a rare attempt to hold alleged polluters accountable in the Democratic Republic of Congo. They are also suing the government, accusing it of failing to enforce environmental regulations.

Like other plaintiffs, she asked NPR not to identify her, fearing retribution from the company or government. Although the claimants' names are public in court documents, they want to avoid further exposure. Their lawyers also fear the plaintiffs could face intimidation from other locals.

"Our children are the first victims," she said, as the sun set over a nearby mound of mine tailings. "What we're hoping for is to see justice done."

The plaintiffs, whose case began Nov. 3, describe similar problems: contaminated water, nosebleeds, skin rashes, miscarriages and birth defects, which they blame on mining pollution.

The mine, known as COMMUS, is owned by Chinese multinational Zijin and lies in Kolwezi, a city of more than 500,000 people in the heart of Congo's copper belt, a southern region with vast mineral reserves.

Congo is the world's second-largest producer of copper, and also the source of over 70% of the world's cobalt, a metal that is critical to the electric-vehicle revolution because of its use in rechargeable batteries.

Last year, the U.S. signed a sweeping economic partnership with Congo aimed at attracting American investment and challenging the dominance of Chinese companies in the country's mining industry

Despite the global importance of Congo's copper and cobalt mines, however, environmental pollution from the industry has received comparatively little scrutiny.

In Kolwezi, pollution is severe. Neighborhoods near mines are often filled with an acrid smell that residents attribute to the sulfuric acid used to process minerals. A study published in June by environmental research organization Source International — carried out with the advocacy groups RAID and Afrewatch, and scientists from Congo's University of Lubumbashi — also highlighted the scale of the contamination.

Researchers found that levels of fine particulate matter, known as PM2.5, in Kolwezi were three to six times the World Health Organization's air quality guideline. The highest concentrations were recorded near the COMMUS mine.

These tiny particles can penetrate deep into the lungs and enter the bloodstream. Exposure poses health risks generally, but is particularly dangerous for pregnant women and young children.

The researchers also tested dust samples and found residue of copper, cobalt and manganese, which they said pointed to mining waste as the main source. When the study was released, Source International's executive director, Flaviano Bianchini, said that "these are among the most concerning air quality results we have documented in years of monitoring pollution at industrial mining sites around the world."

The study did not examine health impacts directly, and the authors recommended formal epidemiological research. Residents and health workers in Kolwezi nonetheless point to a string of ailments that they blame on a polluted environment.

In a dilapidated health clinic in the shadow of a mountain of waste from the COMMUS mine, nurse Héritier Bukassa said that people routinely break out in itchy hives. "Some sick people scratch themselves with knives to relieve itching," he explained.

Bukassa added that women in the area also suffer from high rates of miscarriage, and that he had referred four babies born with congenital malformations — mostly cleft palates — to hospitals this year alone.

Respiratory illnesses are common too, Bukassa said, especially in otherwise healthy babies who develop breathing problems a few weeks after birth. "No one from the [mining] company has ever come to talk to us about this," the nurse said.

Zijin, the owner of COMMUS, did not respond to emailed requests for comment. Neither did Congo's mining and environment ministries.

The Cobalt Institute, an industry lobby, said that understanding environmental pollution requires "an evidence-based approach that considers all potential sources and contributors." It added that companies perform environmental monitoring and carry out mitigation measures.

RAID, which is supporting the plaintiffs alongside Afrewatch, described the case this month as one of "the most ambitious legal challenges yet brought by Congolese residents over industrial mining pollution."

The suit is an important test case that could lead to communities challenging other mines in the future, it added.

The plaintiffs are seeking $1.3 million in compensation for health problems and medical expenses, as well as $5 million to restore the environment. Their lawyers say they worry their clients might come under pressure or intimidation to withdraw their testimony.

The mother, however, said she had no such fears. "We have a right to a clean environment," she said, "and to health."

text:
Washington, D.C. – Congressman Andrew R. Garbarino (R-NY) led a letter to Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) Administrator Lee Zeldin urging the agency to swiftly reinstate the Solar for All program following two federal court rulings rejecting the program's termination. The effort seeks to restore $7 billion in congressionally approved funding intended to lower electricity bills and strengthen the nation's energy grid.

The Solar for All program was established to help more than 900,000 households nationwide reduce their electricity bills by at least 20 percent. New York was awarded nearly $250 million through the program, funding that would help expand access to affordable energy for families across the state, including on Long Island.

“At a time when families on Long Island and across the country are struggling with rising electricity bills, we should be doing everything we can to bring costs down,” said Rep. Garbarino. “Solar for All is an opportunity to deliver real savings for American families while supporting domestic manufacturing, creating jobs, and strengthening our energy independence. Congress already approved this funding, and states are ready to put it to work. We should be focused on getting these projects moving, not standing in the way of affordable American energy.”

Congress appropriated $7 billion for Solar for All, and the EPA fully obligated those funds before terminating the program in August 2025. Two federal district courts have since ruled against the termination, reaffirming Congress's intent for the program to move forward.

In their letter, Garbarino and his Republican colleagues emphasize that restoring the program is consistent with an all-of-the-above American energy strategy. Beyond lowering household electricity bills, Solar for All was designed to expand domestic manufacturing, strengthen American supply chains, create jobs, and improve grid reliability as electricity demand continues to rise.

Garbarino urged Administrator Zeldin to act quickly to allow states, territories, and tribes to resume implementation of their approved projects and deliver the benefits of the program to American families.

"This letter from Rep. Garbarino and House Republican colleagues makes clear what American families stand to gain from the Solar for All program: lower energy bills and new jobs. Now, it's time for EPA to release the funding so that states, tribes, and territories nationwide can move forward with much-needed projects,"said Nick Torrey, Senior Attorney, Southern Environmental Law Center.

"Solar for All would deliver meaningfully lower energy costs for more than 900,000 households. It would also build a local clean energy workforce and strengthen grid resilience. We applaud Congressman Garbarino and his colleagues for urging the reinstatement of these critical funds. Their continued leadership shows that solar belongs in any all-of-the-above energy strategy," said Erin Duncan, Vice President of Congressional Affairs at the Solar Energy Industries Association.

"At a time when American families are struggling with rising costs, affordable energy is more important than ever. Solar for All offers a practical way to lower household bills, create good-paying local jobs, and put more money back into communities. Restoring the program would give states and businesses the certainty they need to bring greater financial stability to more families," said Doug Edwards, President, Exact Solar.
